decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Animal Anatomy and Physiology
decks.description: Explain integrated animal function through transport and feedback.

includes: Comparative tissues and organs, circulation, respiration, digestion, renal regulation, endocrine and neural control and reproduction

practice: Explain a combined exercise, dehydration or temperature perturbation using anatomical diagrams, transport calculations and feedback predictions.

outcomes.description: Explain neural, muscular and endocrine coordination from membrane excitability through organ responses and interpret perturbation time courses.
Explain digestive, metabolic, renal, osmotic and thermal regulation using mass balances and negative-feedback diagrams across animal adaptations.
Compare reproductive systems, hormonal cycles and life-history strategies and relate their regulation to whole-organism energy and environmental constraints.
Identify major tissues and organ relationships and calculate bounded pressure-flow, diffusion and gas-exchange models with explicitly taught physiological parameters.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Biochemistry and Metabolism
decks.description: Connect biomolecular structure to catalysis and metabolic function.

includes: Macromolecules, enzyme models, bioenergetics and major metabolic pathways
excludes: Electronic-structure derivations and full metabolic-network dynamics

practice: Diagnose an enzyme perturbation from rate curves and construct a carbon, electron and energy budget for a metabolic condition.

outcomes.description: Use an explicitly taught Michaelis-Menten model and inhibition variants to estimate parameters by graphical or grid comparison and explain assumptions and limitations.
Represent protein, nucleic-acid, carbohydrate and lipid structures and explain folding, binding and membrane assembly through chemical interactions.
Track atoms, electrons, ATP and chemical gradients through glycolysis, respiration, photosynthesis and major biosynthetic routes; explain regulation and compartmentation.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Molecular and Cellular Biophysics
decks.description: Connect molecular energy landscapes and stochastic motion to biological measurements.

includes: Binding and folding thermodynamics, polymer mechanics, stochastic molecular dynamics and single-molecule inference
excludes: Novel instrument engineering and atomistic electronic calculations

practice: Fit competing energy-landscape models to supplied single-molecule data and use predicted perturbation responses to distinguish them.

outcomes.description: Construct discrete-state kinetic and overdamped diffusion models for conformational transitions, motors and molecular transport with explicit fluctuation assumptions.
Derive binding, folding, cooperativity and polymer elasticity models from partition functions and compare free-energy and structural interpretations.
Infer energies, rates and states from taught force-spectroscopy, fluorescence-transfer and correlation measurements and test time-resolution, calibration and identifiability limits.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Cell Biology
decks.description: Explain cellular organization and responses through mechanistic models.

includes: Membranes, organelles, transport, cytoskeleton, signaling, cell cycle and imaging interpretation

practice: Construct competing explanations of a trafficking or cell-cycle phenotype and specify imaging and perturbation results that would discriminate them.

outcomes.description: Explain membrane transport, organelle function, protein targeting, vesicular trafficking and cytoskeletal mechanics using spatial and energy-flow representations.
Explain cell-cycle control, division, adhesion and cell death; distinguish mechanisms from microscopy and intervention time courses.
Trace receptor, second-messenger and kinase pathways and infer feedback or cross-talk from perturbation and localization evidence.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Ecological Forecasting and Conservation
decks.description: Forecast ecological change and justify conservation actions under uncertainty.

includes: Structured populations, imperfect detection, spatial ecology, ecosystem change and conservation decisions

practice: Build a transparent conservation assessment for a fragmented landscape, including detection-aware estimates, forecasts and stakeholder tradeoffs.

outcomes.description: Compare restoration, reserve and harvesting scenarios through projected outcomes, uncertainty, biodiversity, climate effects and competing community obligations.
Construct stage-structured matrix population models and estimate survival, abundance and occupancy with explicitly taught detection likelihoods.
Analyze metapopulation connectivity, landscape fragmentation and ecosystem carbon or nutrient budgets using spatial data and bounded dispersal models.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Developmental Biology
decks.description: Explain how spatially organized organisms emerge from regulated cell behavior.

includes: Fate specification, pattern formation, lineage, morphogenesis, regeneration and developmental inference

practice: Reconstruct a developmental mechanism from lineage and perturbation data and propose a time-resolved discriminating experiment.

outcomes.description: Infer developmental causality from lineage tracing, mosaics, transplantation, temporal perturbation and live imaging while distinguishing fate from survival effects.
Relate cell division, migration, adhesion, mechanics and death to tissue morphogenesis, stem-cell maintenance and regeneration.
Explain competence, induction, positional information and gene-regulatory patterning using comparative embryonic and plant developmental examples.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Disease Ecology and Epidemiology
decks.description: Infer disease dynamics and compare interventions using biological and population evidence.

includes: Transmission models, study designs, causal bias, surveillance and intervention analysis

practice: Analyze a supplied outbreak with both transmission and observational models and defend an intervention while exposing causal and surveillance limitations.

outcomes.description: Analyze cohort, case-control and surveillance data using risks, odds and standardized comparisons; use taught causal diagrams to diagnose confounding, selection and measurement bias.
Compare intervention scenarios through explicit parameter-grid fitting and uncertainty propagation and justify choices involving equity, resistance, privacy and ecological effects.
Derive SIR and vector or reservoir models, calculate reproduction thresholds and analyze vaccination, immunity and contact-structure effects.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Ecology
decks.description: Explain ecological patterns with population models and field evidence.

includes: Population growth, life tables, species interactions, food webs, nutrient cycles and field sampling

practice: Collect or audit field observations and compare demographic and interaction-based explanations of an unfamiliar abundance pattern.

outcomes.description: Explain competition, predation, mutualism, succession, food webs and carbon, nitrogen and energy budgets using explicit ecological representations.
Design quadrat, transect and mark-recapture sampling; estimate abundance and diversity and assess detection, spatial sampling and observational confounding.
Calculate discrete population projections, life-table reproduction and bounded exponential and logistic growth; state density-dependence and closed-population assumptions.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Evolution and Phylogeny
decks.description: Explain biological change and reconstruct relationships from evidence.

includes: Selection, drift, migration, speciation, phylogenetic reconstruction and macroevolutionary evidence

practice: Reconstruct a small tree and compare selection and drift explanations of an unfamiliar population dataset.

outcomes.description: Evaluate evidence for adaptation, speciation, homology, extinction and major evolutionary transitions, including fossils, comparative traits and historical contingency.
Construct small phylogenies by parsimony and compare supplied finite-state substitution likelihoods using explicitly taught branch probabilities and ancestral-state summation.
Calculate Hardy-Weinberg expectations and discrete allele-frequency changes under selection and migration; represent drift by binomial sampling and distinguish evolutionary mechanisms.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Evolutionary Theory
decks.description: Derive and infer evolutionary processes from population and genealogical models.

includes: Forward population models, fixation, quantitative genetics, coalescent genealogy and demographic inference
excludes: General diffusion-limit proofs and specialized frontier population genomics

practice: Implement forward and coalescent simulations and infer a demographic scenario while testing whether selection or structure gives indistinguishable evidence.

outcomes.description: Construct neutral coalescent waiting-time and branching models and compare recombination, structure and changing population size through simulation.
Estimate demographic or selective parameters from summary statistics or bounded likelihoods and test confounding, model fit and historical identifiability.
Derive Wright-Fisher and Moran transitions, fixation and mutation-selection balances and quantitative-genetic response models under explicit population assumptions.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Biological Experimentation
decks.description: Generate interpretable biological observations through controlled methods.

includes: Microscopy, volumetric technique, sterile handling, DNA extraction, PCR and gels, controls and ethical study design
excludes: Unsupervised human, animal or pathogen procedures

practice: Run a controlled microscopy or nonhazardous DNA-assay study with a preregistered analysis, complete controls and an ethical alternatives assessment.

outcomes.description: Specify biological versus technical replication, randomization, blinding, endpoints and sample handling; analyze effects using descriptive and resampling methods.
Justify a study design by comparing welfare, consent, biosafety, data stewardship, environmental impact and evidential value.
Calibrate microscopy and pipetting, use aseptic technique, and explain and execute bounded DNA extraction, PCR and gel protocols with positive and negative controls.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Foundations of Living Systems
decks.description: Explain living systems through organization, ancestry and testable evidence.

includes: Cellular organization, organismal diversity, evolution, biological scales and evidence
excludes: Detailed molecular mechanisms and clinical practice

practice: Construct an evidence-annotated comparison of unfamiliar organisms and propose a test distinguishing two explanations of a trait.

outcomes.description: Compare bacteria, archaea, protists, fungi, plants and animals using cellular features, life cycles and evolutionary relationships.
Separate observations, hypotheses and mechanisms; propose controls and competing explanations for a simple biological observation.
Identify cells, tissues, organs, organisms and ecosystems in diagrams and images; distinguish matter, energy and information flows.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Genetics
decks.description: Infer inheritance mechanisms from crosses and family evidence.

includes: Chromosomes, meiosis, Mendelian and non-Mendelian inheritance, linkage, pedigrees and genetic variation

practice: Infer competing genetic models for an unfamiliar pedigree and cross dataset and design a discriminating follow-up cross.

outcomes.description: Relate meiosis and chromosome segregation to Mendelian, sex-linked, cytoplasmic and non-Mendelian inheritance and calculate cross and pedigree probabilities.
Infer linkage, recombination order and map distances from crosses; distinguish complementation, epistasis and allelism with explicit experiments.
Explain mutation, chromosome variation and genotype-environment interaction; interpret penetrance, expressivity and quantitative-trait evidence without genetic determinism.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Genomics and Bioinformatics
decks.description: Infer biological structure and function from genome-scale sequence evidence.

includes: Sequence alignment, assembly, annotation, variants, expression, phylogenomics and reproducible pipelines

practice: Implement a small alignment engine and analyze an unfamiliar sequencing dataset through a versioned, quality-controlled biological inference pipeline.

outcomes.description: Execute and audit read quality control, mapping, graph-based assembly, annotation and variant-calling workflows, distinguishing algorithm implementation from tool use.
Analyze expression counts and sequence relationships with normalization, multiple-testing control, phylogenetic uncertainty and biological validation.
Implement pairwise alignment dynamic programming and hidden-Markov forward and Viterbi procedures with explicitly defined emissions, transitions and scoring models.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Immunology
decks.description: Explain immune specificity and regulation through cell and molecular evidence.

includes: Innate recognition, inflammation, adaptive receptors, selection, antigen presentation, tolerance and immune assays

practice: Analyze an unfamiliar immune-response dataset and design controls separating cell abundance, specificity and functional activation.

outcomes.description: Explain receptor diversification, antigen presentation, lymphocyte selection, clonal expansion, memory and tolerance using cellular interaction diagrams.
Trace barrier, innate-recognition, complement and inflammatory responses and connect cytokine signals to cell recruitment and pathogen control.
Interpret flow-cytometry gates, antibody assays and functional perturbations in vaccination, infection, allergy, autoimmunity and tumor immunity.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Microbiology and Virology
decks.description: Identify microbial functions and interpret culture and infection evidence.

includes: Microbial diversity, culture and identification, metabolism, growth, horizontal transfer, viruses and host interactions

practice: Characterize safe unknown isolates or supplied datasets with growth, identity and susceptibility controls and defend identification uncertainty.

outcomes.description: Compare bacterial, archaeal, fungal and protist structures, metabolism and ecological roles and combine staining, biochemical and sequence evidence for identification.
Measure microbial growth and viable counts, distinguish batch phases and nutrient limitation and explain gene transfer, biofilms and antimicrobial susceptibility assays.
Compare viral genome and replication strategies, transmission and host interactions and interpret plaque, molecular and resistance evidence.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Molecular Biology
decks.description: Explain and experimentally manipulate biological information flow.

includes: Replication, repair, transcription, RNA processing, translation, regulation and molecular manipulation

practice: Design a bounded gene-regulation experiment from sequence through construct, controls, assay and predicted alternative outcomes.

outcomes.description: Trace DNA replication and repair, transcription, RNA processing and translation with sequence polarity, molecular interactions and error-control mechanisms.
Design primers, cloning and genome-editing constructs and interpret sequencing, reporter and expression assays with specificity and off-target controls.
Compare prokaryotic and eukaryotic gene regulation, chromatin and epigenetic mechanisms using reporter, binding and expression evidence.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Neuroscience
decks.description: Connect neural activity, circuitry and behavior using experimental evidence.

includes: Membrane excitability, synapses, sensory and motor circuits, learning and neural recording evidence
excludes: Large-scale neural model fitting and clinical intervention

practice: Analyze recordings and perturbations from an unfamiliar sensory circuit and propose a test separating encoding from causal function.

outcomes.description: Trace sensory, motor and autonomic pathways and explain circuit motifs, plasticity, memory and behavioral control across neural scales.
Calculate equilibrium potentials using the explicitly taught Nernst model and explain action potentials, synaptic transmission and excitation-inhibition integration.
Interpret voltage-clamp, extracellular, imaging, lesion and perturbation evidence; distinguish tuning, correlation, necessity and sufficiency.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Plant Biology
decks.description: Connect plant organization, physiology and environmental adaptation.

includes: Plant anatomy, life cycles, water and mineral transport, photosynthesis, hormones and stress responses

practice: Analyze a plant water-stress experiment and connect measured anatomy, gas exchange and growth to alternative physiological explanations.

outcomes.description: Explain meristems, hormonal regulation, photoperiodism and stress responses and design experiments distinguishing growth and signaling mechanisms.
Identify plant tissues, organs and major lineages and compare alternation-of-generations and reproductive structures.
Calculate bounded water-potential and transpiration models and explain xylem, phloem, mineral nutrition and C3, C4 and CAM carbon acquisition.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Quantitative and Systems Biology
decks.description: Construct and test quantitative mechanisms for biological dynamics.

includes: Reaction networks, deterministic and stochastic dynamics, feedback, parameter inference and model discrimination

practice: Implement deterministic and stochastic gene-network models and use perturbation data to test parameter and mechanism identifiability.

outcomes.description: Fit dynamic models using explicitly taught sensitivity equations and least-squares or likelihood objectives; assess identifiability, uncertainty and perturbation-based model discrimination.
Translate biochemical and regulatory diagrams into stoichiometric ODE models and analyze conservation, steady states, feedback and bifurcation examples.
Derive discrete reaction propensities and implement the Gillespie direct method; compare stochastic distributions with deterministic concentration trajectories.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Structural Biology
decks.description: Use structural evidence to recover and validate macromolecular models.

includes: Macromolecular coordinates, diffraction and image formation, crystallography, cryo-EM, NMR restraints and structural validation
excludes: Quantum derivations of spectroscopy and development of reconstruction algorithms

practice: Use supplied diffraction, image or restraint data to build a bounded structural model, script its geometric analysis and report independent validation.

outcomes.description: Explain finite Fourier image and diffraction models, reciprocal space, phase ambiguity and projection geometry; execute taught crystallographic, cryo-EM or restraint-based reconstruction workflows.
Manipulate molecular coordinates and rigid transformations; calculate distances, angles, contacts and least-squares structural superpositions.
Assess resolution, map-model agreement, stereochemistry, cross-validation and conformational heterogeneity and distinguish experimentally constrained structure from model assumptions.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Synthetic Biology and Biotechnology
decks.description: Engineer biological functions and evaluate their reliability and consequences.

includes: Genetic circuits, pathway engineering, design-build-test cycles, burden, robustness and containment
excludes: Unapproved environmental release and clinical engineering

practice: Complete a model-backed design-build-test proposal or authorized safe implementation with quantitative specifications and escape and containment tests.

outcomes.description: Translate a functional specification into genetic logic, feedback or metabolic-pathway models and predict performance and resource burden.
Design constructs, host choices, assembly and assay workflows and use perturbation-driven iteration to improve expression, flux or dynamic behavior.
Evaluate stability, evolutionary escape, reproducibility, containment and dual-use or environmental consequences and justify a bounded deployment decision.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Computational and Systems Neuroscience
decks.description: Model neural dynamics and infer their relationship to computation and behavior.

includes: Conductance and spiking models, neural networks, plasticity, encoding, decoding and mechanistic validation

practice: Implement a neural dynamical model and decoder and challenge both with held-out recordings and simulated causal interventions.

outcomes.description: Fit neural encoding models and Bayesian decoders using taught likelihoods; assess held-out predictions, latent-state ambiguity and causal perturbation evidence.
Construct recurrent spiking and rate networks with synaptic plasticity and analyze stability, oscillation and stimulus-response predictions.
Derive and simulate passive cable, conductance-based and integrate-and-fire models, using explicitly taught compartment discretization and channel-state assumptions.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Advanced Synthesis and Catalysis
decks.description: Develop evidence-based catalytic and stereoselective synthesis strategies.

includes: Organometallic catalysis, asymmetric synthesis, mechanistic evidence and complex-route strategy

practice: Propose a catalytic route to an unfamiliar stereochemical target and use supplied kinetics and spectra to defend or revise its mechanism.

outcomes.description: Construct and discriminate catalytic cycles using elementary organometallic steps, rate laws, isotope effects and intermediate spectroscopy.
Predict and compare asymmetric catalytic, auxiliary and substrate-controlled selectivity using transition-state models and stereochemical evidence.
Defend a complex-target synthesis against alternatives using step economy, selectivity, robustness, supply, safety, waste and analytical feasibility.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Analytical and Instrumental Chemistry
decks.description: Select, execute and validate instrumental chemical measurements.

includes: Chromatography, electrophoretic separation, optical and mass spectrometry, NMR, electroanalysis and method validation
excludes: Quantum derivation of spectra and advanced pulse sequences

practice: Analyze an unknown mixture with separation and two complementary detection methods, including calibration and a defensible uncertainty budget.

outcomes.description: Explain signal generation and instrument blocks for UV-visible, IR, NMR, mass and electrochemical methods; acquire and interpret bounded qualitative and quantitative data.
Select chromatographic and electrophoretic separations; calculate retention, resolution, partition effects and sample recovery with explicit instrument models.
Design calibration, internal-standard, blank and spike-recovery procedures; calculate detection limits and assess matrix effects, selectivity and orthogonal confirmation.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Atomic Structure and Bonding
decks.description: Explain molecular shape and qualitative properties through electronic structure.

includes: Shells and orbitals, periodic trends, Lewis structures, geometry, qualitative molecular orbitals and intermolecular forces

practice: Compare competing bonding models for unfamiliar molecules and defend property predictions with explicit diagrams.

outcomes.description: Assign electron configurations and explain atomic spectra and periodic trends using quantized shells and orbital representations without deriving wave equations.
Construct Lewis, resonance, VSEPR, hybridization and qualitative molecular-orbital diagrams; predict geometry, bond order, polarity and magnetism.
Relate intermolecular forces and bonding types to solubility, boiling behavior and molecular or solid properties, identifying model limitations.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Computational Chemistry
decks.description: Perform reproducible molecular calculations with model and convergence audits.

includes: SCF implementation, DFT and correlated-method use, geometry optimization, molecular simulation and free-energy estimation

practice: Implement a small SCF solver and complete a molecular free-energy comparison with reproducible convergence and model-sensitivity studies.

outcomes.description: Implement a small-basis Hartree-Fock SCF calculation from supplied integrals; explain and compare DFT and correlated-method calculations without claiming to implement them.
Optimize molecular geometries and transition-state candidates and execute force-field dynamics and free-energy sampling with explicitly taught estimators and ensemble controls.
Assess basis, functional, force-field, finite-size and sampling errors and validate predicted energies, structures and observables against independent evidence.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Dynamics
decks.description: Connect molecular motion and energy landscapes to reaction and relaxation rates.

includes: Transition-state theory, collision models, reaction-diffusion, surface catalysis and nonadiabatic rate models

practice: Compare measured rate-temperature and transport data with competing molecular and diffusion-limited models and identify their decisive assumptions.

outcomes.description: Derive collision and transition-state rate expressions from partition functions and compare barrier, entropy, tunneling and recrossing effects.
Construct adsorption-reaction catalytic models and analyze elementary Marcus or avoided-crossing nonadiabatic rates using explicitly derived local assumptions.
Derive bounded one-dimensional reaction-diffusion and diffusion-limited encounter models and compare kinetic-control and transport-control regimes.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Environmental Chemistry
decks.description: Explain chemical fate and assess interventions in environmental systems.

includes: Air-water-soil chemistry, speciation, transport-reaction budgets, contaminants, sampling and remediation judgment

practice: Investigate a supplied contamination case with speciation calculations, a compartment model, a sampling plan and a justified intervention comparison.

outcomes.description: Design defensible sampling and compare remediation choices using effectiveness, uncertainty, exposure, ecological burden and environmental-justice consequences.
Construct compartment mass balances with partitioning, first-order reaction and exchange; calculate persistence, speciation and exposure under explicit assumptions.
Explain atmospheric photochemistry, aquatic carbonate and redox systems and soil sorption using chemical mechanisms and analytical evidence.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Equilibria and Electrochemistry
decks.description: Calculate chemical speciation and equilibrium responses with bounded models.

includes: Mass-action models, acid-base and solubility equilibria, mass and charge balance, redox and electrochemical cells

practice: Predict a mixed solution's titration and precipitation behavior and verify all proposed species concentrations against conservation constraints.

outcomes.description: Calculate pH, buffers, titration curves, solubility and coupled aqueous speciation using mass and charge balances and checked approximations.
Set up reaction quotients and equilibrium balances; use Gibbs-energy and equilibrium-constant relations with stated ideal-solution assumptions.
Balance redox reactions and calculate cell potentials, Nernst responses and electrolysis quantities; distinguish thermodynamic favorability from reaction rate.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Inorganic Chemistry
decks.description: Relate inorganic structure, electronic configuration and reactivity.

includes: Main-group trends, coordination chemistry, ligand fields, inorganic solids and elementary organometallic cycles
excludes: Advanced quantum calculations and catalytic synthesis strategy

practice: Identify plausible coordination structures from magnetic and spectral evidence and audit electron counts through a catalytic cycle.

outcomes.description: Represent coordination geometry and isomerism; calculate d-electron counts and ligand-field splitting and interpret color, magnetism and substitution tendencies.
Predict main-group structures and reactions using periodic trends, acid-base concepts, oxidation states and representative compound families.
Describe unit cells and ionic or network solids and perform electron counting in elementary organometallic catalytic cycles.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Kinetics
decks.description: Infer reaction rates and discriminate mechanistic explanations.

includes: Rate laws, integrated kinetics, initial-rate analysis, elementary mechanisms, catalysis and temperature dependence

practice: Fit candidate integrated laws by explicit parameter scans or linearized formulas, inspect residuals and design a mechanism-discriminating experiment.

outcomes.description: Construct elementary-step rate equations and derive pre-equilibrium and steady-state approximations for consecutive, parallel and catalytic mechanisms.
Determine rate laws from initial-rate and concentration-time data; derive zero-, first- and second-order integrated laws and estimate parameters with residual checks.
Estimate Arrhenius activation parameters, distinguish rate and equilibrium effects and diagnose transport or temperature-control confounding.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Laboratory Practice
decks.description: Perform reliable basic chemical operations and defend safe experimental choices.

includes: Weighing, volumetry, solution preparation, filtration, extraction, distillation, titration and laboratory records

practice: Prepare and assay an unknown solution, document mass balance and defend the safest adequate separation and waste procedure.

outcomes.description: Execute standardized titrations and gravimetric assays using supplied indicator chemistry; calculate blanks, calibration, recovery and uncertainty.
Maintain traceable records and compare procedural alternatives using hazard, exposure, incompatibility, waste, reproducibility and environmental evidence.
Select and perform weighing, volumetric preparation, filtration, extraction and simple distillation with documented recovery and contamination controls.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Materials and Polymer Chemistry
decks.description: Relate chemical processing and structure to material performance.

includes: Polymer formation, molecular-weight distributions, solid and nanomaterial synthesis, interfaces and energy materials

practice: Develop a synthesis-characterization plan for a specified polymer or electrode and reconcile structure, processing and property measurements.

outcomes.description: Analyze adsorption, surface chemistry, colloidal stability and electrochemical energy-material behavior using isotherms, charge balances and complementary characterization.
Select routes for crystalline, amorphous and nanoscale materials and interpret diffraction through locally taught reciprocal-spacing and Bragg relations plus thermal and imaging evidence.
Compare step-growth and chain-growth polymerization, calculate conversion and molecular-weight measures and relate architecture to thermal and mechanical behavior.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Matter and Chemical Reactions
decks.description: Connect particles, chemical formulas and measurable reaction quantities.

includes: Atomic composition, chemical notation, mole calculations, reaction balances, gases and phases
excludes: Detailed orbital theory and equilibrium calculations

practice: Plan quantities for a reaction and reconcile theoretical yield with measured gas or mass data.

outcomes.description: Interpret elements, isotopes, ions, formulas and common chemical names; distinguish substances, mixtures and physical versus chemical changes.
Use the ideal-gas model and particle representations to calculate gas quantities and explain phases, solutions and departures from ideality qualitatively.
Balance atoms and charge, assign oxidation states, and calculate moles, concentrations, limiting reagents, yields and dilution.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organic Reaction Mechanisms
decks.description: Predict organic transformations from mechanistic reasoning.

includes: Electron-pushing mechanisms, substitution, elimination, addition, aromatic and carbonyl reactions and selectivity

practice: Predict and defend products for unfamiliar substrates and design isotope or stereochemical evidence that distinguishes mechanisms.

outcomes.description: Use curved-arrow electron bookkeeping, acid-base equilibria, nucleophilicity and intermediate stability to construct chemically valid mechanisms.
Predict substitution, elimination, alkene addition, aromatic substitution and carbonyl addition or substitution pathways under specified conditions.
Explain regio-, stereo- and chemoselectivity and distinguish kinetic and thermodynamic control using reaction-coordinate diagrams and competing pathways.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organic Structure and Identification
decks.description: Represent three-dimensional organic molecules and identify simple structures.

includes: Organic functional groups, conformations, stereochemistry and introductory IR, proton NMR and mass spectra
excludes: Advanced reaction mechanisms and multidimensional spectra

practice: Identify an unknown small molecule from combined spectra and defend its stereochemical representation using physical or digital models.

outcomes.description: Assign simple structures using taught IR group frequencies, proton-NMR shifts, integration and first-order splitting, plus molecular-ion and isotope patterns.
Construct wedge-dash, Newman and chair representations; assign stereodescriptors and distinguish enantiomers, diastereomers and conformational populations qualitatively.
Translate names, formulas, skeletal structures and functional groups; compare constitutional isomers and resonance representations.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Quantum Chemistry
decks.description: Derive approximate molecular structure and energy from quantum mechanics.

includes: Electronic Hamiltonians, antisymmetry, Born-Oppenheimer separation, variational orbitals and molecular transitions

practice: Construct a small variational molecular calculation and predict vibrational or electronic transitions with an explicit approximation audit.

outcomes.description: Construct atomic and molecular electronic Hamiltonians, antisymmetrized states and variational matrix problems; derive the Hartree-Fock approximation and its limitations.
Apply Born-Oppenheimer separation and molecular symmetry to bonding, potential-energy surfaces, rotations and harmonic vibrations.
Calculate transition moments, elementary selection rules and rotational, vibrational and electronic spectral spacings from approximate states.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Advanced Molecular Spectroscopy
decks.description: Derive molecular spectral signals and infer structure and dynamics.

includes: Light-matter response, rotational and vibrational spectra, Raman, electronic spectra, spin resonance and inverse assignments

practice: Derive a bounded spin or vibrational spectrum and resolve an unfamiliar molecular assignment with complementary experimental evidence.

outcomes.description: Combine complementary spectra to infer structure, conformational exchange and reaction intermediates while testing assignment ambiguity and instrument limitations.
Construct spin Hamiltonians and analyze NMR and EPR shifts, couplings, relaxation and bounded two-dimensional pulse experiments.
Derive transition intensities, polarization selection and line-shape models for rotational, vibrational, Raman and electronic spectra.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organic Synthesis
decks.description: Plan and evaluate practical multistep organic syntheses.

includes: Retrosynthesis, carbon-carbon bond formation, enolates, organometallic reagents, pericyclic patterns and route execution
excludes: Advanced catalytic strategy for complex total synthesis

practice: Design and, where authorized, execute a short synthesis with intermediate identification and a defended alternative route.

outcomes.description: Plan reagents, workups, purification and structural checkpoints; calculate cumulative yield and compare waste, hazards and scalability.
Apply enolate, organometallic, oxidation-reduction and elementary pericyclic methods with explicit selectivity and orbital-symmetry models.
Decompose targets into strategic disconnections and functional-group interconversions while managing protecting groups and convergent route alternatives.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Thermodynamics
decks.description: Derive and apply thermodynamics to reactions and nonideal mixtures.

includes: Thermodynamic potentials, chemical potentials, activities, partial molar quantities and phase diagrams
excludes: Molecular simulation and nonequilibrium reaction theory

practice: Infer a nonideal binary phase diagram from free-energy data and predict reaction equilibrium under changed temperature and pressure.

outcomes.description: Calculate partial molar quantities, activities, fugacities and mixing free energies; relate equilibrium constants to temperature and pressure.
Construct and interpret unary and binary phase diagrams, common tangents, phase-rule constraints and coupled reaction-phase equilibria.
Derive thermodynamic potentials, Maxwell relations and chemical potentials using total differentials and Legendre transformations.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Advanced Algorithms
decks.description: Develop algorithms with rigorous guarantees for difficult problems.

includes: Network flows, approximation, randomized algorithms, online analysis and relaxation methods

practice: Design and prove an approximation or streaming algorithm, then test the sharpness of its bound on constructed instances.

outcomes.description: Derive flow, matching and approximation algorithms using relaxations, rounding and primal-dual constructions and prove their guarantees.
Analyze online and streaming algorithms through adversarial examples, competitive ratios and memory lower-bound arguments for bounded models.
Design randomized algorithms and sketches and prove success probabilities and resource bounds with concentration and amplification.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Advanced Machine Learning
decks.description: Develop and critically evaluate probabilistic and sequential learning systems.

includes: Generalization theory, deep representation learning, variational generative models, sequence models and reinforcement learning

practice: Implement a generative or sequential learner, derive its objective and compare predictive, sampling or decision performance against transparent baselines.

outcomes.description: Prove bounded finite-class generalization and stability results and analyze regularization, optimization bias and representation choices under stated assumptions.
Derive variational lower bounds and implement a latent-variable generative model and an attention-based sequence model with explicit likelihood and sampling procedures.
Derive Bellman equations and implement dynamic programming, temporal-difference and policy-gradient methods; evaluate exploration, off-policy bias, safety and reward misspecification.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Data Structures and Algorithms
decks.description: Design efficient algorithms with explicit correctness arguments.

includes: Data structures, sorting, graph algorithms, greedy methods, dynamic programming and asymptotic analysis

practice: Implement alternative route-planning algorithms, prove their guarantees and benchmark carefully chosen adversarial graphs.

outcomes.description: Prove correctness with invariants and induction and derive worst-case, expected and amortized time-space bounds for standard structures and algorithms.
Implement sorting, graph traversal, shortest paths, spanning trees, greedy and dynamic-programming solutions using explicit state and recurrence definitions.
Implement and compare arrays, linked structures, hash tables, heaps, balanced search-tree operations and disjoint sets.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Architecture
decks.description: Explain how programs execute on digital hardware.

includes: Boolean circuits, binary arithmetic, instruction sets, assembly, pipelines, caches and memory representation

practice: Build a small CPU emulator and compare cache traces for two implementations of the same computation.

outcomes.description: Construct combinational and sequential logic, finite-state controllers and binary arithmetic circuits, including signed and floating-point representations.
Trace instruction execution and calling conventions in assembly; build a small instruction-set emulator and explain pipeline hazards.
Analyze memory layout, pointers, caches and locality and predict the performance consequences of access patterns.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Symbolic Artificial Intelligence
decks.description: Represent and solve symbolic reasoning and planning problems.

includes: State-space search, heuristics, adversarial search, constraints, logic and planning
excludes: Statistical learning and continuous probabilistic inference

practice: Build a planner for an unfamiliar scheduling or navigation domain and compare search, constraint and logical formulations.

outcomes.description: Formulate and solve constraint-satisfaction problems with propagation, backtracking and variable-order heuristics.
Represent facts and actions in propositional and first-order fragments; implement unification, inference and classical planning with explicit soundness boundaries.
Implement uninformed, heuristic and adversarial search and prove admissibility-based guarantees for bounded state-space problems.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Compiler Construction
decks.description: Translate a language into executable code while preserving meaning.

includes: Lexing, parsing, semantic analysis, intermediate representations, optimization and code generation

practice: Build a small optimizing compiler and demonstrate differential testing, correct control flow and measured optimization effects.

outcomes.description: Implement instruction selection, register allocation and calling conventions and validate generated code against an interpreter and adversarial tests.
Implement tokenization, recursive-descent and table-driven parsing, symbol resolution and type checking for a specified language.
Construct control-flow and SSA intermediate representations and implement dataflow analysis and semantics-preserving local optimizations.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Theory of Computation
decks.description: Establish the limits and resource costs of computation.

includes: Automata, grammars, Turing machines, undecidability, reductions and complexity classes

practice: Classify a new language family and give a complete reduction proof for a constrained decision problem.

outcomes.description: Classify decision problems using P, NP, coNP and space classes; prove NP-completeness with explicit polynomial reductions and certificates.
Construct Turing-machine and enumeration arguments and prove undecidability using diagonalization and mapping reductions.
Construct finite automata, regular expressions, context-free grammars and pushdown machines; prove equivalence and nonexpressibility claims.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Database Systems
decks.description: Design reliable persistent representations and query them efficiently.

includes: Relational modeling, SQL, normalization, indexes, query plans, transactions and recovery
excludes: Distributed consensus and large-scale search infrastructure

practice: Build a normalized reservation database and test concurrent bookings, rollback and alternative indexed query plans.

outcomes.description: Translate requirements into entity relationships and relational schemas; use keys, functional dependencies and normalization to prevent anomalies.
Write joins, aggregation and nested SQL queries; explain relational algebra, B-tree and hash indexes and cost-based query plans.
Analyze transaction schedules, isolation, locking and write-ahead recovery and implement application-level integrity and rollback tests.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Distributed Systems
decks.description: Build services that remain interpretable under partial failure.

includes: Failure models, ordering, consistency, replication, consensus, distributed transactions and observability

practice: Build a replicated key-value service and test its claimed consistency during message loss, partitions and process crashes.

outcomes.description: Model asynchronous failures, clocks and causality; distinguish linearizability, serializability and eventual consistency and explain consensus impossibility assumptions.
Design sharding, observability and failure-injection tests; compare availability, consistency, latency and operational complexity with measured evidence.
Implement replicated logs and a bounded crash-fault consensus protocol; analyze quorums, partitions, retries and distributed transaction recovery.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Formal Methods and Verification
decks.description: Turn behavioral requirements into checkable correctness claims.

includes: Hoare logic, invariants, temporal specifications, model checking, SMT and mechanized proof

practice: Specify a stateful protocol, implement a small model checker and mechanize a complementary invariant proof.

outcomes.description: Implement explicit-state reachability and use a taught SAT/SMT encoding procedure to verify bounded systems and interpret counterexamples.
Write preconditions, postconditions, loop invariants and temporal safety or liveness specifications with explicit environment assumptions.
Prove program-correctness and refinement claims in Hoare or operational logic and encode a small proof in an introduced proof assistant.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Graphics and Geometric Vision
decks.description: Construct images from geometry and infer geometry from images.

includes: Three-dimensional geometry, projection, rasterization, ray tracing, image filtering and geometric reconstruction
excludes: Production animation and learned vision architectures

practice: Implement a small renderer and reconstruct a calibrated tabletop scene, comparing image artifacts and recovered geometry against ground truth.

outcomes.description: Represent meshes, homogeneous transformations and cameras and calculate projection, clipping, barycentric interpolation and visibility.
Implement image convolution, camera calibration and two-view triangulation and estimate geometric parameters by linear least squares with reprojection checks.
Implement rasterization and ray intersection with explicitly taught local lighting and reflectance models; compare sampling, filtering and aliasing artifacts.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Human-Computer Interaction
decks.description: Design and evaluate interactive systems around human capabilities and obligations.

includes: Task analysis, interaction design, accessibility, prototyping, usability studies and responsible design

practice: Prototype two interfaces, conduct an approved task study and revise the design using accessibility and privacy evidence.

outcomes.description: Plan usability and comparative studies, collect task and qualitative evidence and analyze completion, errors and uncertainty without overclaiming.
Analyze users and tasks and construct accessible interaction flows and prototypes using feedback, consistency, error recovery and cognitive-load principles.
Justify design choices involving disability access, privacy, consent, manipulation, cultural context and competing stakeholder needs.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Programming Languages
decks.description: Define and implement programming-language meaning.

includes: Syntax, operational semantics, lambda calculus, environments, type systems and interpreters

practice: Specify a small typed language, build its interpreter and prove type safety for its expression fragment.

outcomes.description: Implement and test interpreters supporting functions, closures and state and compare functional, imperative and object-oriented abstractions.
Specify abstract syntax and small- and big-step semantics; compare substitution, environments, evaluation order, mutation and lexical scope.
Construct typing rules and type inference for a small language and prove representative progress and preservation lemmas by structural induction.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Machine Learning
decks.description: Learn predictive representations and validate their generalization.

includes: Supervised and unsupervised models, graphical inference, neural networks, regularization and responsible evaluation
excludes: Advanced sequential and generative learning theory

practice: Implement representative models from their equations and compare them on an unfamiliar dataset with held-out, subgroup and calibration audits.

outcomes.description: Use leakage-free validation, regularization, calibration and error analysis and assess distribution shift, subgroup performance, privacy and deployment consequences.
Derive backpropagation and implement small neural networks; perform finite graphical-model variable elimination and expectation-maximization for taught latent-variable models.
Implement regression, classification, trees, kernels, clustering and principal-component models and select losses and representations appropriate to data and tasks.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Networks
decks.description: Build networked applications and diagnose packet-level behavior.

includes: Layered protocols, framing, addressing, routing, transport, congestion and socket applications
excludes: Distributed consensus and information-theoretic coding proofs

practice: Implement a robust file-transfer protocol over sockets and explain its behavior under injected loss, delay and malformed messages.

outcomes.description: Trace messages through link, network, transport and application layers, including framing, addressing, checksums, name resolution and connection establishment.
Execute distance-vector and link-state routing procedures and analyze retransmission, flow control, congestion and throughput under simple delay-loss models.
Implement framed socket clients and servers with timeouts and partial-read handling; capture and diagnose protocol exchanges.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Operating Systems
decks.description: Explain and implement resource-management and concurrency mechanisms.

includes: Processes, threads, synchronization, virtual memory, scheduling, filesystems, I/O and protection

practice: Implement a concurrent storage service and test race conditions, memory pressure and recovery after injected crashes.

outcomes.description: Trace address translation, paging and allocation and compare replacement policies, protection boundaries and memory-resource tradeoffs.
Analyze process and thread lifecycles, scheduling, synchronization, races and deadlocks; implement bounded concurrent programs with locks and condition variables.
Explain filesystem allocation, caching, device I/O and crash consistency and implement a small filesystem or storage-layer model.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Parallel and High-Performance Computing
decks.description: Implement correct parallel computations and explain measured performance.

includes: Parallel models, shared and distributed memory, accelerator kernels, synchronization and scaling analysis

practice: Parallelize a matrix or graph workload in two execution models and explain correctness and scaling limits through profiles.

outcomes.description: Implement shared-memory, message-passing and accelerator kernels with explicit synchronization, partitioning and memory-access reasoning.
Analyze work, span, speedup and communication costs and select task, data and pipeline decompositions.
Profile locality, contention, load imbalance and transfer overhead; establish numerical or functional equivalence and reproducible scaling measurements.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Programming Foundations
decks.description: Develop and debug small reproducible programs from specifications.

includes: Variables, expressions, control flow, functions, recursion, collections, files, command-line use and tests

practice: Implement a file-processing application with malformed-input handling, unit tests and a reproducible execution guide.

outcomes.description: Use a command-line environment, exceptions, assertions, tests and a debugger to isolate errors and document reproducible execution.
Write programs using numeric and text values, conditionals, loops, functions and terminating recursion; trace state and scope.
Represent records with lists, maps and simple objects; parse, validate and transform text and structured files.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Quantum Information and Computation
decks.description: Analyze quantum computational constructions and their noise limitations.

includes: Qubits, circuits, quantum algorithms, density matrices, channels and elementary error correction

practice: Implement a finite quantum algorithm and a small error-correcting code, proving ideal guarantees and measuring performance under specified noise.

outcomes.description: Implement state-vector simulations of amplitude amplification and phase estimation and prove their bounded success and query-complexity guarantees.
Construct tensor-product qubit circuits, controlled gates and measurements; derive entanglement, teleportation and circuit-equivalence results.
Define density matrices, partial traces and quantum channels locally and analyze simple noise models and stabilizer error-correction codes.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Robotics
decks.description: Integrate geometry, inference and control for embodied agents.

includes: Rigid transformations, robot kinematics, Bayesian localization, mapping, planning and feedback integration

practice: Implement a simulated robot's localization, collision-free planning and tracking stack and quantify failures under sensor and actuator perturbations.

outcomes.description: Derive and implement Kalman and particle-filter localization from motion and sensor likelihoods and analyze observability and map uncertainty.
Construct homogeneous rigid transformations, forward and inverse manipulator kinematics and Jacobians and identify singular configurations.
Implement configuration-space collision checking, sampling-based paths and feedback tracking and assess uncertainty, actuator limits and safety envelopes.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Security
decks.description: Analyze adversarial failures and engineer justified defenses.

includes: Threat modeling, memory and web vulnerabilities, authentication, cryptographic constructions, defense and incident analysis
excludes: Unauthorized exploitation and cryptographic research proofs

practice: Audit and harden an isolated application, demonstrate mitigations with regression tests and produce an evidence-based incident and disclosure report.

outcomes.description: Explain security games and attack probabilities; use authenticated encryption, hashes, signatures and key exchange through audited libraries and explicitly taught toy modular examples.
Harden services with least privilege, validation, secrets management and monitoring; investigate logs and justify disclosure, privacy and residual-risk decisions.
Construct threat models and demonstrate memory, injection, authorization and protocol failures in isolated authorized examples.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Software Engineering
decks.description: Turn stakeholder needs into maintainable, verified software increments.

includes: Requirements, modular and object-oriented design, interfaces, testing, version control, review and professional tradeoffs

practice: Develop a small team service through changing requirements, reviewed commits, automated tests and a documented ethical design decision.

outcomes.description: Plan reproducible delivery and maintenance; justify decisions involving reliability, licensing, privacy, accessibility, technical debt and stakeholder harm.
Elicit testable requirements and design modular interfaces, data models and object collaborations with explicit invariants and failure behavior.
Use unit, integration and property-based testing, refactoring, code review and version-control workflows to manage evolving software.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Abstract Algebra
decks.description: Recognize and prove structural relationships in algebraic systems.

includes: Groups, actions, homomorphisms, rings, ideals, polynomial factorization and field extensions
excludes: General Galois theory and homological algebra

practice: Classify an unfamiliar quotient structure and construct a finite field with proved arithmetic and extension properties.

outcomes.description: Construct finite and simple algebraic field extensions and calculate degrees, minimal polynomials and vector-space bases.
Analyze groups, subgroups, cosets, actions and quotient groups and prove homomorphism and finite-group structure results.
Work with rings, ideals, quotient rings, divisibility and polynomial factorization; prove basic isomorphism and unique-factorization claims.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Real Analysis
decks.description: Prove the foundations and validity conditions of limiting arguments.

includes: Completeness, rigorous limits, metric spaces, compactness, continuity, differentiation and uniform convergence
excludes: Measure integration and general functional analysis

practice: Prove a convergence theorem with minimal hypotheses and construct counterexamples when each key hypothesis is removed.

outcomes.description: Prove differentiation and Riemann-integration results and determine when uniform convergence permits exchanging limits, integrals and derivatives.
Use real-number completeness, epsilon arguments and subsequences to prove convergence and construct counterexamples.
Prove metric-space continuity, compactness, completeness and connectedness results, including the contraction-mapping theorem.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Single-Variable Calculus
decks.description: Calculate rates, accumulation and local approximations.

includes: Limits, derivatives, integration, fundamental theorem, infinite series and Taylor approximation
excludes: Multivariable calculus and rigorous completeness arguments

practice: Derive a rate-and-accumulation model and compare exact integration, approximation and graphical reasoning.

outcomes.description: Evaluate limits and derivatives, use chain and implicit differentiation, and solve rate, extrema and local linearization problems.
Interpret definite integrals as limits of sums, apply the fundamental theorem and use substitution, parts and improper integration.
Test convergence of elementary sequences and series and construct Taylor approximations with justified remainder estimates.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Combinatorics and Graph Theory
decks.description: Prove counting, existence and extremal results for finite structures.

includes: Generating functions, extremal graphs, matching, probabilistic existence and algebraic counting

practice: Solve one enumeration problem and one extremal existence problem with complete proofs and a small computational check.

outcomes.description: Derive ordinary and exponential generating functions and use recurrences, coefficient extraction and inclusion-exclusion to count constrained structures.
Prove matching, coloring, connectivity and extremal graph results and use adjacency matrices to count walks and expose structure.
Use first- and second-moment arguments and elementary concentration to prove existence and bound random-structure behavior.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Complex Analysis
decks.description: Use complex structure to prove and calculate analytic relationships.

includes: Holomorphic functions, Cauchy theory, series, residues, conformal maps and contour applications

practice: Evaluate a parameterized real integral by contours and solve a planar potential problem using a justified conformal map.

outcomes.description: Test holomorphicity, derive Cauchy-Riemann relations and prove core consequences of Cauchy's theorem and integral formula.
Evaluate real integrals and count zeros by complex methods; construct elementary conformal maps and interpret harmonic potentials.
Construct Taylor and Laurent expansions, classify singularities and calculate contour integrals with residues and branch choices.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Data and Uncertainty
decks.description: Reason responsibly from small datasets and uncertain measurements.

includes: Descriptive statistics, finite probability, elementary regression, sampling and uncertainty using explicit formulas and resampling procedures

practice: Audit a noisy dataset, reproduce a bootstrap interval by the stated resampling steps and critique an unsupported causal claim.

outcomes.description: Calculate finite sample-space, conditional and Bayes probabilities, expected values and binomial probabilities under stated independence assumptions.
Summarize and visualize data, calculate means, spread and least-squares lines from finite sums, and interpret residuals and outliers.
Distinguish sampling bias, randomization and causation; execute bootstrap and permutation procedures with a provided tool and interpret intervals and tests.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Differential Equations and Dynamics
decks.description: Solve and analyze deterministic evolution models.

includes: First- and second-order ODEs, linear systems, phase planes, stability and numerical stepping concepts
excludes: General PDEs and stochastic differential equations

practice: Solve a forced two-state system and compare analytical predictions, phase portraits and hand-computed numerical steps.

outcomes.description: Formulate initial-value models and solve separable, first-order linear and constant-coefficient second-order equations with forcing.
Analyze nonlinear equilibria by linearization and phase portraits; explain uniqueness, stability, bifurcation examples and Euler-step limitations.
Solve linear systems using eigenstructure and matrix exponentials, including repeated eigenvalues; compare modes and transient behavior.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Differential Geometry
decks.description: Calculate geometric quantities independently of coordinate choice.

includes: Smooth manifolds, tangent and cotangent spaces, differential forms, metrics, connections, geodesics and curvature

practice: Compute geodesics and curvature for an unfamiliar two-dimensional metric and verify tensorial consistency under a coordinate change.

outcomes.description: Calculate Riemann, Ricci and scalar curvature for specified metrics and relate curvature to parallel transport, geodesic deviation and surface topology.
Construct smooth charts, tangent maps, vector fields and differential forms and apply manifold integration and Stokes' theorem.
Transform tensors and metrics between coordinates and derive covariant derivatives, Levi-Civita connections and geodesic equations.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Proof and Discrete Foundations
decks.description: Construct rigorous arguments and discrete representations.

includes: Logical notation, proof methods, sets, relations, finite graphs, counting and recurrences
excludes: Advanced graph theory and abstract algebra

practice: Prove a graph invariant, solve a counting problem two ways and identify the exact failure in a plausible false proof.

outcomes.description: Count finite configurations using bijections, inclusion-exclusion and binomial coefficients; solve elementary recurrences and use divisibility and modular arithmetic.
Work with sets, functions, equivalence relations, orders, Boolean algebra, graphs and trees; prove elementary structural properties.
Translate quantified statements and prove claims by direct argument, contradiction, contrapositive and induction; construct counterexamples.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Quantitative Foundations
decks.description: Represent and solve quantitative problems with explicit units and assumptions.

includes: Arithmetic, units, equations, coordinates, trigonometry, functions and complex-number notation

practice: Model a scaling and measurement problem from prose, graph its predictions and check units and limiting cases.

outcomes.description: Calculate with fractions, ratios, powers, scientific notation and units; solve linear and quadratic equations and inequalities.
Translate between formulas, tables and graphs; use exponential, logarithmic and trigonometric functions and rectangular and polar complex numbers.
Use Cartesian coordinates, similar triangles, area, volume, radians, trigonometry and vector components in two and three dimensions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Graduate Algebra
decks.description: Use structural algebra across extensions, modules and symmetry representations.

includes: Modules, tensor products, exact sequences, Galois theory and finite-group representations
excludes: Advanced arithmetic and derived algebraic geometry

practice: Compute a splitting field and character table and compare the structural roles of field, module and representation viewpoints.

outcomes.description: Determine splitting fields and Galois groups and prove the correspondence between intermediate fields and subgroups in finite Galois extensions.
Construct modules, tensor products and exact sequences and prove structure results over principal ideal domains with explicit universal properties.
Decompose finite-group representations using characters and prove orthogonality and complete reducibility under appropriate field assumptions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Graduate Probability and Stochastic Calculus
decks.description: Analyze random evolution with rigorous limiting and integration methods.

includes: Conditional expectation, modes of convergence, martingales, Brownian motion, Ito integration and diffusion equations
excludes: Rough paths and general stochastic PDEs

practice: Derive and simulate a diffusion's stationary and hitting behavior and justify every limiting or optional-stopping step.

outcomes.description: Construct conditional expectation through measure and projection arguments and prove relationships among convergence modes and standard limit results.
Define Ito integration, derive Ito's formula and solve elementary SDEs; connect generators, Fokker-Planck equations and Euler-Maruyama validation.
Prove bounded martingale convergence and stopping results with explicit hypotheses and construct Brownian motion properties from Gaussian increments.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Linear Algebra
decks.description: Represent linear structure and solve forward and inverse linear problems.

includes: Real and complex finite-dimensional vector spaces, systems, transformations, orthogonality and decompositions

practice: Recover an unknown vector from noisy linear observations and diagnose ambiguity using null spaces and singular values.

outcomes.description: Construct bases and matrix representations of linear maps; explain span, independence, dimension, coordinate changes and inner products.
Calculate eigenvalues, orthogonal projections, least-squares solutions and singular-value decompositions; interpret conditioning and symmetric or Hermitian spectral structure.
Solve linear systems by elimination; interpret rank, null spaces, determinants and existence or nonuniqueness of solutions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Measure Theory and Functional Analysis
decks.description: Control infinite-dimensional limits and linear approximation rigorously.

includes: Measures, Lebesgue integration, convergence, product measures, Lp spaces, Banach and Hilbert spaces and operators

practice: Prove an interchange-of-limits result and formulate a Hilbert-space inverse problem with existence, approximation and stability analysis.

outcomes.description: Define Lebesgue integrals and Lp spaces and prove monotone, dominated and Fubini convergence results and Radon-Nikodym applications.
Construct measures and measurable functions and prove extension, almost-everywhere and product-measure results in standard settings.
Analyze bounded operators, duality, weak convergence and Hilbert projections; prove core Banach-space principles and compact self-adjoint spectral results.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Multivariable and Vector Calculus
decks.description: Calculate with fields and coordinate-dependent quantities in several dimensions.

includes: Partial derivatives, Jacobians, multiple integrals, coordinate transformations and vector integral theorems

practice: Compute mass and flux for a three-dimensional region in two coordinate systems and verify an integral theorem.

outcomes.description: Calculate partial and directional derivatives, gradients, Jacobians and Hessians; use multivariable chain rules and local extrema tests.
Calculate line and surface integrals, divergence and curl; apply Green, Gauss and Stokes theorems with orientation and regularity conditions.
Evaluate multiple integrals in Cartesian, polar, cylindrical and spherical coordinates with correct Jacobians and domain bounds.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Number Theory
decks.description: Prove arithmetic properties and justify number-theoretic procedures.

includes: Congruences, quadratic residues, Diophantine equations, arithmetic functions and computational number theory
excludes: Analytic prime-distribution theory and advanced arithmetic geometry

practice: Solve an unfamiliar Diophantine problem and produce a verifiable arithmetic certificate rather than relying on a black-box result.

outcomes.description: Execute and justify modular exponentiation, primality tests and elementary factorization procedures; distinguish proof certificates from probabilistic evidence.
Analyze arithmetic functions, continued fractions and elementary Diophantine equations using divisibility, descent and algebraic norms.
Prove and apply Chinese remaindering, multiplicative-order results, quadratic reciprocity and congruence solvability criteria.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Numerical Methods
decks.description: Implement reliable numerical algorithms and assess their errors.

includes: Floating-point error, conditioning, root finding, interpolation, quadrature, linear solvers, Fourier transforms and ODE integration

practice: Build a tested numerical library and document failure cases caused separately by conditioning, roundoff and discretization.

outcomes.description: Implement bracketed and Newton root solvers, interpolation, quadrature, direct and iterative linear solvers and a discrete fast Fourier transform.
Analyze floating-point rounding, conditioning, stability and forward versus backward error using testable numerical examples.
Implement Runge-Kutta and implicit ODE steps; assess consistency, stability, stiffness, adaptive error estimates and convergence by refinement.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Optimization
decks.description: Formulate and solve constrained decisions with justified optimality claims.

includes: Linear and nonlinear programming, convexity, duality, optimality conditions and implementable algorithms

practice: Model a resource-allocation problem, implement two solvers and verify primal feasibility, dual bounds and sensitivity.

outcomes.description: Implement gradient, Newton, projected and simplex methods; compare stopping criteria, conditioning and bounded smooth-convex convergence arguments.
Derive Lagrange and KKT conditions and linear-program duality; prove convex sufficiency and interpret complementary slackness and sensitivity.
Translate allocation, estimation and control objectives into linear, convex and nonlinear programs and distinguish feasibility, local and global solutions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Partial Differential Equations
decks.description: Solve and validate spatially evolving and equilibrium field models.

includes: Elliptic, parabolic and hyperbolic equations, characteristics, Fourier methods, weak solutions and numerical discretization

practice: Solve a two-dimensional boundary-value problem analytically where possible and implement a convergent discretization with an energy-based error argument.

outcomes.description: Classify PDEs and formulate initial and boundary conditions; derive conservation, characteristic and energy arguments for well-posedness in standard models.
Solve heat, wave, Laplace and transport equations in one to three dimensions using separation, Fourier transforms, characteristics and Green functions.
Construct Sobolev weak formulations and finite-difference or piecewise-linear finite-element schemes; prove bounded energy estimates and assess stability and convergence.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Probability
decks.description: Construct probabilistic models and derive their consequences.

includes: Discrete and continuous distributions, joint laws, conditioning, moments and classical limit theorems

practice: Derive and numerically check the distribution of a transformed measurement and assess a normal approximation's error.

outcomes.description: Calculate joint and conditional laws, covariance and conditional expectations using finite sums and iterated integrals defined for joint densities.
Construct probability mass and density functions, transform random variables and calculate expectations, variances and common distribution probabilities.
Apply and explain laws of large numbers, central-limit approximations and elementary concentration bounds with their assumptions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Statistical Inference
decks.description: Make and validate quantitative inferences from designed and observational data.

includes: Likelihood, Bayesian inference, testing, linear and generalized linear models, design and diagnostics
excludes: Specialized causal identification and general statistical-learning theory

practice: Analyze a randomized study and an observational dataset, implement one estimator and report model failures and inferential limits.

outcomes.description: Design randomized and blocked comparisons and analyze interactions, missingness, multiplicity and selection; implement resampling and report uncertainty reproducibly.
Derive likelihood and conjugate Bayesian estimates, confidence and credible intervals, tests and power for standard models; explain coverage and prior sensitivity.
Fit linear and generalized linear models using matrix least squares and explicitly taught score/Hessian iteration; diagnose residuals, collinearity and misspecification.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Stochastic Processes
decks.description: Predict and simulate random evolution with accessible state-based models.

includes: Discrete and continuous-time Markov chains, Poisson and renewal processes, queues and simulation
excludes: Measure-theoretic martingale convergence and stochastic integration

practice: Implement a queue or birth-death simulator and independently verify its transient and stationary predictions.

outcomes.description: Analyze finite Markov-chain transition matrices, communicating classes, stationary laws, hitting probabilities and mean passage times.
Construct Poisson, renewal, birth-death and elementary queue models; calculate generators, transient probabilities and stationary performance.
Implement inverse-transform, categorical and event-driven sampling and compare empirical transition and waiting-time statistics with analytical predictions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Topology
decks.description: Distinguish spaces through continuous structure and elementary invariants.

includes: Topological spaces, products and quotients, compactness, connectedness, homotopy and fundamental groups
excludes: Higher homotopy theory and smooth curvature

practice: Analyze a quotient surface and prove that two proposed spaces cannot be homeomorphic using an appropriate invariant.

outcomes.description: Construct product, subspace and quotient topologies and describe surfaces through polygon identifications and explicit continuous maps.
Calculate elementary fundamental groups using homotopy and van Kampen's theorem; use covering examples to distinguish spaces.
Prove continuity, compactness, connectedness and separation properties in topological spaces and compare metric and nonmetric examples.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Advanced Electrodynamics
decks.description: Solve general classical field problems with causality and boundary structure.

includes: Boundary Green functions, multipoles, retarded fields, radiation, waveguides and covariant electrodynamics

practice: Calculate radiation from a localized time-dependent source and independently verify its boundary, far-field and energy-conservation limits.

outcomes.description: Solve electrostatic and wave boundary problems with Green functions, multipole expansions and waveguide modes and check uniqueness and boundary conditions.
Construct electromagnetic four-vectors and field tensors, derive their Lorentz transformations and express conservation and gauge freedom covariantly.
Derive retarded potentials and calculate dipole and accelerated-charge radiation, angular distributions, scattering and energy flux.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Advanced Quantum Theory
decks.description: Calculate interacting quantum processes and formulate many-particle descriptions.

includes: Symmetry and angular momentum, time-dependent perturbation, scattering, density operators, identical particles and second quantization

practice: Calculate a transition and scattering cross section and compare first- and second-quantized formulations of a simple many-particle model.

outcomes.description: Construct bosonic and fermionic Fock spaces and second-quantized Hamiltonians and derive elementary path-integral and many-body mean-field descriptions.
Derive time-dependent transition rates, Born and partial-wave scattering and resolvent or Green-function formulations with controlled approximations.
Construct rotation representations and coupled angular momenta, use symmetry selection rules and analyze mixed states through density operators and partial traces.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Analytical Mechanics
