decks.description: Exploit coordinates, symmetries and phase space to analyze mechanics.

includes: Variational principles, constraints, symmetries, Hamiltonian dynamics, canonical transformations and perturbative mechanics

practice: Derive and reduce a constrained multi-coordinate system, then compare conserved quantities and perturbative trajectories.

outcomes.description: Construct Hamiltonians, Poisson brackets and canonical transformations and solve elementary Hamilton-Jacobi and action-angle problems.
Derive Euler-Lagrange equations from variations, incorporate holonomic constraints and connect continuous symmetries to conserved quantities.
Analyze small oscillations, weak perturbations and elementary chaotic maps or driven systems using phase-space structure and stability diagnostics.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Astrophysics and Astronomy
decks.description: Connect astronomical observations to physical models and hidden parameters.

includes: Photometry, spectra, distance inference, radiative transfer, stellar structure, galaxies and planetary systems
excludes: General relativity and telescope engineering certification

practice: Infer properties of an unfamiliar stellar or exoplanet system from calibrated observations and compare competing physical explanations.

outcomes.description: Calibrate photometric and spectral data and infer distance, temperature, velocity and composition using magnitudes, parallax, Doppler shifts and taught line-formation models.
Derive bounded radiative-transfer and stellar hydrostatic models; explain energy generation, stellar evolution and compact-object limits.
Analyze orbital and transit evidence, galaxy rotation and population diagrams and distinguish parameter degeneracy, selection effects and model disagreement.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Computational Physics
decks.description: Implement physical simulations with independent accuracy and conservation checks.

includes: Particle integration, symplectic stepping, Monte Carlo, finite differences and numerical validation

practice: Produce reproducible dynamical, diffusion and sampling experiments with independent error budgets rather than visual plausibility checks.

outcomes.description: Implement particle and molecular dynamics with pair forces, Verlet stepping and boundary conditions and compare energy drift and timestep dependence.
Implement Monte Carlo integration and Metropolis sampling; derive detailed balance for proposed moves and estimate autocorrelation-adjusted uncertainty.
Implement bounded one-dimensional diffusion finite differences and verify stability, conservation and grid convergence against analytical solutions.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Condensed-Matter Physics
decks.description: Infer collective material behavior from microscopic models and measurements.

includes: Lattices, reciprocal space, phonons, bands, transport, magnetism, superconductivity and experimental signatures
excludes: Device-process engineering and exhaustive many-body frontier methods

practice: Infer a solid's likely electronic and collective behavior from a calculated band model and unfamiliar thermal, diffraction and transport data.

outcomes.description: Derive Bloch, tight-binding and nearly-free-electron models and calculate band filling, semiconductor statistics and bounded transport responses.
Construct real and reciprocal lattices and calculate diffraction conditions, lattice vibrations and phonon contributions to thermal properties.
Analyze elementary magnetic, superconducting and topological-band models and compare their order parameters and transport or spectral signatures.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Control and System Identification
decks.description: Identify and regulate dynamical systems using measurements and feedback.

includes: State-space and transfer models, Laplace transforms, identification, stability, feedback and observers

practice: Identify a low-voltage thermal or motor plant and implement feedback with documented stability and actuator-limit tests.

outcomes.description: Design PID, pole-placement and observer-based feedback; assess stability, margins, saturation and sampled implementation through simulation and measurements.
Estimate low-order plant parameters from step and frequency-response data using least squares and residual checks; distinguish noise and unmodeled dynamics.
Derive state-space and transfer-function models using locally developed Laplace transforms; calculate poles, frequency responses, controllability and observability.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Classical Dynamics
decks.description: Derive and solve classical motion models beyond constant acceleration.

includes: Calculus-based particle motion, gravitation, rotation, coupled oscillations and noninertial frames
excludes: Variational mechanics and general nonlinear ODE theory

practice: Predict a coupled pendulum or rotating-body response and compare measured normal modes or angular momentum with the model.

outcomes.description: Derive vector equations of motion, central-force effective potentials and orbital relations; apply conservation and rotating-frame forces.
Solve harmonic, damped and driven oscillators by taught exponential trial solutions and diagonalize small coupled-oscillator systems.
Calculate centers of mass and inertia tensors and analyze torque, angular momentum, rolling and elementary gyroscopic motion.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Electricity and Magnetism
decks.description: Calculate fields and electromagnetic responses from sources and boundaries.

includes: Electrostatics, magnetostatics, potentials, materials, circuit transients and Maxwell equations
excludes: General radiation and relativistic field calculations

practice: Solve a field-boundary problem and predict the transient and energy flow of a coupled electromagnetic circuit.

outcomes.description: Derive capacitance, inductance and RC, RL and RLC responses; connect field energy, induction and circuit energy balances.
Apply differential and integral Maxwell equations, derive vacuum plane waves and calculate polarization, Poynting flux and boundary reflection.
Calculate electric and magnetic fields and potentials in three dimensions using source integrals, symmetry and elementary conductor or dielectric boundary conditions.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Fluid Mechanics
decks.description: Model continuum motion and transport across physical and biological settings.

includes: Continuum balances, stress, Navier-Stokes equations, dimensional analysis, viscous flows and transport

practice: Derive a channel-flow model, compare analytical and supplied numerical solutions and infer viscosity from pressure-flow observations.

outcomes.description: Derive integral and differential mass, momentum and energy balances; relate Newtonian stress to velocity gradients and derive Navier-Stokes equations.
Solve hydrostatic, potential, pipe, creeping and elementary boundary-layer flows and identify Reynolds-number regimes and similarity scalings.
Formulate advection-diffusion and heat-transport models, interpret turbulence closures and validate a provided flow solver through balances and mesh comparisons.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Laboratory Measurement and Electronics
decks.description: Build measurement chains and interpret their electrical and statistical limitations.

includes: Calibration, uncertainty, DC and sinusoidal circuits, bounded RC models, diodes, transistors, op-amps and data acquisition
excludes: Maxwell-field derivations and advanced device fabrication

practice: Construct a calibrated temperature or light measurement chain and report bandwidth, residuals, uncertainty and electrical safety decisions.

outcomes.description: Solve resistor networks with Kirchhoff laws and equivalent circuits; calculate sinusoidal impedances and RC step responses from explicitly taught component models.
Design and test rectifier, transistor-switch and op-amp sensor circuits; explain loading, saturation, filtering, sampling and aliasing with bounded models.
Calibrate sensors, use meters and oscilloscopes, propagate independent uncertainty by stated sensitivity formulas, and distinguish systematic error, noise and resolution.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Physical Modeling and Mechanics
decks.description: Build accessible algebraic models of motion and interactions.

includes: Units, motion graphs, constant-acceleration models, free-body diagrams, momentum and energy

practice: Predict and measure a projectile or cart trajectory, then compare force, momentum and energy explanations of discrepancies.

outcomes.description: Apply work-energy, momentum and impulse balances to collisions and motion, stating system boundaries and dissipative assumptions.
Construct free-body diagrams and apply Newton's laws to equilibrium, friction, circular motion and connected-body problems.
Translate positions and motion graphs into displacement, average velocity and acceleration; calculate constant-acceleration trajectories in one and two dimensions.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Modern Physics
decks.description: Recognize and calculate the first departures from classical physics.

excludes: General relativity and full quantum state-space theory

practice: Explain an unfamiliar electron or photon experiment quantitatively and compare classical and bounded quantum predictions.

outcomes.description: Use explicitly derived Bohr and one-dimensional standing-wave models to calculate atomic or confined-particle energies and identify their limitations.
Calculate photoelectric, Compton and matter-wave effects and explain how interference and detection constrain particle and wave descriptions.
Derive and apply Lorentz transformations, invariant intervals and relativistic energy-momentum relations to clocks, collisions and particle lifetimes.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Nuclear and Particle Physics

includes: Nuclear structure, decay, reactions, particle symmetries, relativistic kinematics and detector inference
excludes: Field-theoretic amplitude derivations and facility operation

practice: Analyze supplied decay or scattering data and compare physical-channel hypotheses after detector and background corrections.

outcomes.description: Explain ionization, scintillation and semiconductor detectors and infer rates, lifetimes and cross sections with efficiency, background and counting uncertainty.
Calculate binding energies, decay chains, reaction thresholds and simple nuclear-model predictions and compare fission, fusion and scattering evidence.
Classify fundamental particles and interactions and apply conservation laws, symmetries and relativistic kinematics to decay and collision channels.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Plasma Physics
decks.description: Choose and analyze particle, fluid and kinetic plasma descriptions.

includes: Charged-particle drifts, plasma scales, fluid and MHD models, kinetic theory, waves and instabilities

practice: Calculate a magnetized plasma's characteristic scales and wave spectrum and explain where a fluid prediction fails kinetically.

outcomes.description: Derive two-fluid and magnetohydrodynamic equations and analyze bounded equilibria, waves and elementary stability criteria.
Formulate Vlasov dynamics, derive linear dispersion and Landau damping with a stated contour prescription and compare kinetic and fluid predictions.
Calculate magnetized particle orbits, guiding-center drifts, Debye screening and collision or collective timescales and assess approximation regimes.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Quantum Field Theory
decks.description: Formulate relativistic quantum fields and calculate controlled perturbative predictions.

includes: Relativistic classical fields, canonical and path-integral quantization, perturbative amplitudes, gauge fields and renormalization
excludes: Quantum gravity and nonperturbative frontier programs

practice: Derive and evaluate a simple field theory's scattering prediction through a stated perturbative order and check symmetry and scale dependence.

outcomes.description: Derive propagators and Feynman rules and calculate tree-level scattering and decay in simple scalar and electromagnetic models.
Derive scalar, spinor and gauge-field equations and conserved currents and construct free-field quantization with explicit commutation or anticommutation relations.
Regularize a representative one-loop integral, identify counterterms and derive a bounded renormalization-group flow and effective-theory interpretation.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Quantum Mechanics

excludes: Relativistic fields and general many-body theory

practice: Predict a spin sequence and a bound-state spectrum and compare exact, variational and perturbative calculations.

outcomes.description: Calculate spin measurements and leading perturbative, variational and WKB estimates; compare assumptions, degeneracy and approximation error.
Construct normalized state vectors and wavefunctions, apply observables and unitary evolution and calculate measurement, commutator and uncertainty relations.
Solve one-dimensional wells, barriers and oscillators and separate the three-dimensional central-potential equation to obtain hydrogenic spectra and angular states.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: General Relativity and Cosmology
decks.description: Relate spacetime geometry to gravitation and cosmological observations.

includes: Equivalence principle, Einstein equations, black-hole and cosmological metrics, geodesics and observational inference

practice: Calculate a relativistic observable for a specified metric and fit a bounded cosmological distance model to supplied data by explicit parameter comparison.

outcomes.description: Derive Friedmann evolution and distance-redshift relations and compare expansion, background-radiation and structure evidence with parameter degeneracies.
Construct stress-energy tensors and derive Einstein-equation motivation and conservation structure, connecting weak fields to Newtonian gravity.
Calculate geodesics, redshift, lensing, horizons and geodesic deviation in specified Schwarzschild and weak-wave spacetimes.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Statistical Physics

excludes: Quantum wavefunction derivations and nonequilibrium field theory

practice: Derive a model's equation of state and susceptibility and compare finite-system fluctuations with a thermodynamic-limit approximation.

outcomes.description: Calculate fluctuations, correlations and response and analyze simple spin models, mean-field transitions and critical-scaling limitations.
Derive microcanonical, canonical and grand-canonical weights and calculate thermodynamic observables from partition functions.
Derive classical, Bose and Fermi occupation laws from explicitly stated state-counting rules and calculate gas and oscillator properties.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Thermal Physics

includes: Temperature, equations of state, thermodynamic laws, engines, phase changes and elementary heat transport
excludes: Microscopic ensemble derivations and multicomponent chemical potentials

practice: Analyze a calorimetry and cooling experiment and compare an actual thermal cycle with its reversible bound.

outcomes.description: Apply temperature, internal energy, heat, work and the first and second laws to closed systems with explicit sign and boundary conventions.
Calculate reversible entropy changes, ideal-gas processes, engine efficiencies and phase-change energy balances; distinguish state functions and path quantities.
Calculate steady conduction and radiative exchange and solve lumped thermal-relaxation models, stating transport coefficients and validity limits.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Waves and Optics

excludes: General PDE theory and quantum optics

practice: Design an imaging arrangement and recover an unknown wavelength from diffraction measurements with uncertainty.

outcomes.description: Calculate two-source and grating interference, single-aperture diffraction and polarization intensities; infer wavelength and resolution with stated approximations.
Construct reflection and refraction rays and calculate image location, magnification and paraxial optical-system behavior.
Represent harmonic traveling and standing waves; define partial derivatives locally and derive the one-dimensional string wave equation and acoustic intensity relations.

practiceNotes: Recall practice maintains definitions, representations, assumptions and method selection; extended proofs, implementations, experimental work and interpretive decisions require separate assessment.
Use cumulative unfamiliar problems, delayed retesting, alternative representations, error analysis and transfer tasks rather than recognition alone.

Programming projects require executable tests, reproducible environments, documented datasets and independent review of correctness; using a library does not establish ability to implement or prove its algorithm.
Experimental work requires appropriate facilities, instrument induction, supervision and local safety procedures. Simulated or supplied data can assess analysis but cannot certify hands-on technique.
Human-participant, animal, genetic, environmental and microbial work requires applicable consent, ethics review, containment and authorization; these conditions are not assumed satisfied.
Security exercises must remain within explicitly authorized isolated systems. Radiation, high voltage, lasers, pressure systems and hazardous chemicals require trained supervision.
Clinical care, regulated diagnostics, environmental release and industrial or facility operation remain outside the authorization granted by this curriculum.
Assessment should include accessibility, uncertainty, reproducibility, environmental consequences and justified tradeoffs where the deck explicitly teaches those judgments.
